messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Y-axis formatting with qplot
parts:
Hi:

This is probably because Date is not of class Date in your data frame. Try this:

# Substitute your read statement here, notice the option
# stringsAsFactors = FALSE at the end

# BTW, what I'm doing below is a way to copy data from your
# e-mail and paste it into an R session. I do not recommend that
# you do this on your data.

dd <- read.table(textConnection("

22 2010-09-09 Cladoceran 10.71052"), header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
closeAllConnections()

# Check the structure of the data frame: observe the classes of each variable
str(dd)
# Convert Date to be of class Date
dd$Date <- as.Date(dd$Date)

# Should have Date as class Date, Class as class character (chr) and
# DryBiomass as numeric (num) [compare this to your data]
str(dd)

# I don't use qplot() much myself, but here is a
# scatterplot using ggplot():
ggplot(dd, aes(x = Date, y = DryBiomass, color = Class)) +
geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_line(size = 1)

If you want the same sizes as mine, then in qplot(), you need to use I(2.5)
and I(1) as the values of size in the qplot() call. Perhaps someone can
contribute the corresponding qplot() code.

Sorry, I don't see what added value a stacked area chart would provide -
it seems to me that a scatterplot is sufficient.

HTH,
Dennis
